t: For payments of principal, interest, taxes, and any other obligations under contracts entered into pursuant to the Public Buildings Purchase Contract Act of 1954 (40 U.S.C. 356), $2,350,000.

fable.w: This section only appropriates money to pay obligations under existing purchase contracts. The tempting reading is that the reference to contracts implies involvement of outside parties, but paying contractual obligations is not consulting or coordinating with anyone outside the federal government before a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation, or right to sue.
fable.s: For payments of principal, interest, taxes, and any other obligations under contracts entered into pursuant to the Public Buildings Purchase Contract Act of 1954

qwen_block.w: This section is a simple appropriation clause authorizing funds for specific payments (principal, interest, taxes) related to existing contracts. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties before a decision is made. It is purely a funding provision.
qwen_block.s: For payments of principal, interest, taxes, and any other obligations under contracts entered into pursuant to the Public Buildings Purchase Contract Act of 1954 (40 U.S.C. 356), $2,350,000.

opus.w: This section only provides $2,350,000 to pay obligations under contracts made under the Public Buildings Purchase Contract Act of 1954. Nothing in it requires consultation, hearings, comment periods, advisory bodies or a right to sue. Contract counterparties outside the government are mentioned only as recipients of payments, not as people who help make a federal decision.
opus.b: The tempting reading is that "contracts entered into" suggests outside companies are involved. That fails because this is only a funding line for payments on existing purchase contracts. Nothing in it has outsiders consult on, comment on, or challenge a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriation clause authorizing funds for payments under existing contracts. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in the decision-making process. The definition explicitly excludes applications for contracts, and this text merely authorizes payment for obligations already incurred.
qwen_chat.s: For payments of principal, interest, taxes, and any other obligations under contracts entered into pursuant to the Public Buildings Purchase Contract Act of 1954 (40 U.S.C. 356), $2,350,000.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "contracts entered into pursuant to the Public Buildings Purchase Contract Act" implies a process where outside parties (contractors) participated in the decision to build or purchase buildings. However, the section itself is merely an appropriation clause authorizing funds for payments under existing contracts. It does not describe the process of selecting contractors, holding hearings, or consulting with the public. The act of paying for a contract is not "participation" in the decision-making sense defined (consultation/coordination before a decision). The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits, grants, or contracts.
